75.title: #Music in the forest
arts: I'm leaving home.
We're on our way to the station.
I'm so excited!
We're standing on the platform waiting for the train to Delamere Forest.
We're here!
What a fantastic place to see my favourite singer Jess Glynne right in the middle of a beautiful forest.
I'm eating a hot dog.
It's very expensive, but it's not very good!
It's getting dark now.
The stage is completely black.
A few people are talking, but most people are quiet.
We're waiting for Jess.
And here she comes!
Everyone is cheering!
What a noise!
Jess isn't on stage.
Is the show over?
No way!
We're all shouting 'more'.
Why are we shouting?
Because we want MORE!
But don't worry.
She's walking back onto the stage.
We're on the train home.
We aren't sitting down.
I don't care.
There are so many people on the train and everybody's a Jess Glynne fan.
We're all singing 'Hold my Hand'.
It's my favourite song.
It's exactly midnight and we're back home.
I'm feeling tired but very happy.
I'm going straight upstairs to bed.

77.title: Musicians around the world
arts: Hello and welcome!
Today we are talking about different music from around the world.
Is there a type of music that you really like?
Phone and tell us.
Our first caller is Liliana.
OK Liliana, what's your favourite music?
Hello! My mother is Mexican and we often go to Mexico.
I love the mariachi music I see there.
There's a group of men and sometimes women and they all stand up playing instruments like guitars, trumpets and violins.
They also wear traditional Mexican hats.
I think they look fantastic.
Yes, thanks Liliana.
And now here's Lewis.
Hi Lewis, tell us what you like.
Hi there.
Well in Indonesia there's this traditional musical performance called gamelan.
They have these orchestras with some very unusual instruments.
They make beautiful sounds and when they all play the musicians wear the same traditional clothes.
Thanks Lewis.
And now let's talk to Jen.
I love African drumming.
I go to a lot of musical festivals and there's always some African drumming.
Is there any African country you like the drumming from most?
Well I like all African drumming but the drummers from Burundi are fantastic and they wear these really cool green, red and white clothes.
They're the colours of the Burundi flag.
Sometimes they also paint their drums in the same colours.
Okay, thank you Jen.

78.title: A teenage DJ
arts: Who are you?
I'm Danny Boyd.
I'm 14 years old and I'm from Luton.
What do you do?
I'm a student at school and at the weekends I work as a DJ.
Wow, that's interesting.
Can you tell us more?
I'm a DJ at a local youth club.
I play every Saturday from 6pm to 10pm.
There's usually about 100 people there.
It's great fun.
I also sometimes play for big crowds in the park and sometimes on the beach too.
What do you like doing in your free time?
I love listening to music and finding new songs to play.
I like watching films and playing games on my VR headset but I hate dancing.
I know that's a strange thing for a DJ to say.
I love watching other people dance but I never dance myself.
What do you like wearing?
I like wearing jeans and a white T-shirt.
I also wear a red cap.
I don't like wearing shirts and trousers.
I wear those every day at school.
Thanks Danny and good luck.
Thank you.
Why don't you come to one of my shows one day?

80.title: Dances around the world
arts: The Tango is the national dance of Argentina, and every year on 11th December people in Buenos Aires celebrate the Day of the Tango.
They do the tango in dance halls, parks and squares all over the city.
The dance is usually performed by a man and a woman.
The man often wears smart trousers and a shirt.
The woman often wears a beautiful dress.
The dance is often very interesting to watch.
The Whirling Dervish is a dance from Turkey.
There is a group of twelve men who dance.
They wear traditional costumes with big skirts.
They often all wear white, but sometimes the skirts are different colours.
There is another group of twelve musicians.
They play traditional Turkish instruments.
As the music plays, the dancers spin around in circles, getting faster and faster.
The dance is very popular with tourists.
There are lots of Irish dances, but perhaps the most famous one is the step dance.
One or more dancers perform the step dance.
The dancers only move their legs.
They move them very quickly.
The top half of the body doesn't move.
Dancers usually wear traditional Irish costumes.
The music they dance to is played by an Irish folk band.
They play instruments like the fiddle and the whistle.

85.title: Kitchen Kids
arts: Harry doesn't want to be a star chef when he's 20.
He wants to be one now.
This is why he's on the TV programme Kitchen Kids.
The ten-year-old New Yorker likes cooking.
He can make fantastic soups and salads, excellent omelettes and the best cakes.
But there are many other children on the show, too.
And they are all very good.
More and more young people are interested in cooking.
Many of them learn it from their parents.
Others watch special cooking videos for children on YouTube.
In many cities, there are special cooking classes for young people.
Some of them are for children from the age of three!
But what must you do to become a star chef?
Of course, it's important that you like cooking and are really good at it.
But there are some rules.
You must be nine years old or more to be on Kitchen Kids.
'We must wash our hands before we start cooking,' Harry says.
'And of course we mustn't put them in our mouths.
A chef doesn't do that!
And we must be very careful with hot plates.'
The show starts.
Harry is excited.
He knows he's an excellent cook.
This time he makes tomato soup, some salad, steak and carrot cake.
The experts in the studio love Harry's food, and he stays on the show.
It's 5 pm.
The show is over.
Harry is happy, and a little tired.
He goes home.
It's time to do his homework.

87.title: Cooking
arts: Can we make some sandwiches, Dad?
Of course you can. No problem.
Would you like some help?
No, we're okay, thanks.
Can we use this cheese, Dad?
No, your mum wants that for the lasagna. Use this cheese.
Okay.
We need some salad in the sandwiches. Have we got any?
There's no cucumber, but there are some tomatoes.
Let's have cheese and tomato sandwiches then.
Cool.
What are you doing, Dad?
I'm putting some peanut butter on the bread. It's tastier than butter.
Don't do that.
Too late.
The thing is, Sally is allergic to nuts.
Oh no. I'm sorry.
Never mind. I can eat these.
And you can make some more.
We can't make any more. We haven't got any more bread.
I know. Can we go for fish and chips, Dad?
Hmm, okay. Yes, we can.
Great.
And can Sally and Max come too?
Yes, of course they can.
But first, we must clean up this mess.
Oh, Dad. We're hungry now. Can we do that later?
No, we can't.

88.title: In a restaurant
arts: Hello. Can I help you?
Hi, yes. We'd like a table for two, please.
Here are the menus.
Thanks.
What would you like to drink?
I'd like an orange juice.
And I'd like water, please.
Great.
Are you ready to order now?
Yes. I'd like the pizza with salad.
Any starters?
No thanks.
Would you like any extra toppings on the pizza? Onion, peppers, or tomatoes?
Some peppers, please.
And what would you like?
I'd like the chicken and chips.
Okay. Is that everything?
Yes. Thank you.
Would you like a dessert?
Yes, please. I'd like the fruit salad with vanilla ice cream.
Me, too.
How are your desserts?
Great.
Would you like any more drinks?
No, thanks. We'd like the bill, please.
Of course.
Thank you.

90.title: Offering and asking for help
arts: Wow! What a great smell!
Thanks, Mum! It's lasagna. It's in the oven and it's almost ready.
Lasagna from the shop?
No, Mum. It's my lasagna.
It's got meat, pepper, mushrooms, cheese, onion, everything.
And we can eat it with a bit of salad.
Oh, right! But we? Who's coming for lunch?
Mark and Chloe. We want to study together this afternoon and have lunch together first.
That's okay, right?
Of course, Joe. But...
But what, Mum?
Well, the thing is, I'd like a nice quiet afternoon.
Oh, don't worry, Mum. After lunch, we plan to study upstairs in my room.
Oh! It's ready!
Be careful, Joe. It's very hot. Can I help you?
It's okay, Mum. I can just... Oh, no! My lasagna! It's all over the floor!
Now what?
Well, first, let's clean it all up. And then, do you and your friends want to go to the new sandwich shop?
Not really. But I've got an idea, Mum. We can just have the salad.
Okay. And you and I can make some chocolate-covered bananas so your friends can have some dessert, too.
Thanks, Mum. You're the best!

92.title: She was the first woman in space
arts: Valentina Tereshkova was born in Russia on 6th March 1937.
Her father was a driver and her mother worked in a factory.
Valentina was a worker in a factory, too.
Her hobby was skydiving and it was her dream to be an astronaut and to go into space.
In 1962, there was a big competition to find new astronauts.
There were 400 people interested in going to space.
The training programme wasn't very easy, but Tereshkova was hardworking.
And she was the lucky one.
Tereshkova's big day was on 16th June 1963, and she was just 26.
The next year, she married Andrian Nikolayev, and Tereshkova was the first woman in space.
The flight was very difficult because there were many technical problems and Tereshkova wasn't very well for most of the flight.
She was in space for three days.
She is the only woman to fly into space alone.
After that, she was very famous all over the world.
Her face was on stamps in many countries.
In the year 2000, there was a big celebration in London, and Valentina Tereshkova was named 'Woman of the Century'.
At the opening ceremony of the Winter Olympics in Russia in 2014, Valentina Tereshkova was one of the carriers of the Olympic flag.
These were very important moments for her.

95.title: A prize-giving at school
arts: Hi Will, how are you? Are you better?
Yes, thanks. I was ill yesterday and the day before but I'm okay now.
Good, I'm pleased.
So yesterday was the prize-giving at school, right? Was it good?
No, it wasn't. Well, not really. There weren't many parents there.
Oh really? There were lots last year. Were all the teachers there?
Of course! The teachers can't choose, can they?
No, and neither can the kids. Anyway, who were the big winners this year?
Well, the best student of the year for the whole school was Sandra Hammond.
Sandra? Was she the best student last year too?
No, she wasn't. It was her brother Tom. This year, Tom was the best sports person in the school.
Oh, the Hammonds! They always win everything! Boring!
I know, but it's okay. They're leaving at the end of term, so next year, who knows? Maybe you!
You're joking of course. I'm never the best at anything.
Well, anyway, guess who the best science student was?
No idea. Andy Clarkson?
No, me!
You? Really? Well done! That's fantastic! I'm proud of you. Was the prize something nice?
Yes, it was. A book about science. I really want to read it.
Good for you, Alice. Well done. Thanks, Will.

96.title: Sports achievers
arts: Yesterday, I was online and I learned about a woman called Amy who walked all around the UK to get money for charity and in winter when there was rain and snow. Do you know any other amazing stories like that?
How about Dee Caffari? She sailed around the world non-stop three times. That's right, three times. Imagine the wind and the rain. Fantastic, eh? Jenny.

OK, well, there's a boy called Jordan Romero from the US. He climbed Mount Everest when he was 13 years old. It's really cold up there, but he managed to get to the top. Only 13. Now that's an achievement. Sam.

My friend Corey Armstrong decided to run a marathon when he was 16. He finished in just over four hours. He enjoyed it a lot, so then he decided to do the marathon in Death Valley in the US. It's so hot there, often more than 40 degrees Celsius. This time he was slower, almost five hours, but I still think it's fantastic. 42 kilometres when it's over 40 degrees. I think he almost died. Martha.

Before 1926, a lot of women tried to swim the cold water of the English Channel from England to France, but they all failed. But in 1926, Gertrude Ederle, an Olympic gold medal swimmer, arrived on an English beach after 14 hours and 31 minutes. She returned to her home in New York a hero. How about that? Mark.

99.title: Statues around the world
arts: There are many wonderful statues all over the world.
Many of them help us to remember the lives of great people.
Rosa Parks
One day in 1965, a bus driver in Alabama in the US asked Rosa Parks to give a man her seat because he was white and she was black.
She said no and the police decided to take her away.
It was a very important moment in the history of black people's rights in the US.
The statue shows Rosa sitting on a rock wearing the same clothes as that day in 1965.
Franz Kafka
Franz Kafka was a writer from Prague.
He was born in 1883.
His books were in German.
In his life, he was not very famous, but now he is.
Many of his stories were very strange.
There's a very unusual statue of him in Prague.
He's sitting on the shoulders of an empty suit.
Os Candango
The Candango were men who travelled from all over Brazil between 1956 and 1960 to build the new capital city of Brazil, Brasilia.
In 1956, 256 men arrived, but before long there were 30,000 who worked hard to build the city.
Brasilia opened in 1960 and this 8 meter high statue to remember the Candango is in the 3 powers square.
The two figures are holding digging tools.
Suzanne Lenglen
At the Roland Garros tennis centre in Paris, there is a court called Suzanne Lenglen.
Lenglen was a famous French tennis player who played from 1914 to 1926.
She was the number one player for many years.
In front of the court is this statue.
Lenglen is jumping with a racket in her hand and she is wearing her famous white dress and headband.

102.title: Dolphins to the rescue
arts: Everyone knows that dolphins are very intelligent animals.
But did you know that many scientists believe there is a special connection between dolphins and humans?
There are lots of stories about dolphins helping humans who are in danger.
Here are two of our favourites.
14-year-old Davide Cecchi was in his father's boat off the southeast coast of Italy when he had an accident and fell into the water.
Davide didn't know how to swim, and his father didn't see him fall, so he didn't stop the boat.
He shouted, but his dad didn't hear him.
Davide got very worried.
Then, very quickly, a dolphin came to help him.
It gave Davide a push back up to the top of the water, and the boy got on to the dolphin's back.
The dolphin took him back to the boat.
When Davide's father saw his son, he pulled him from the water.
The dolphin saved Davide's life.
In 2016, Adam Walker went to New Zealand to swim across the Cook Strait between the North and South Islands.
He was swimming when he saw a large dark shape below him.
He knew that it was a great white shark and his life was in danger.
Adam knew he didn't have a lot of time.
A few seconds later, a group of ten dolphins joined him and swam in a circle between him and the shark.
The circle of dolphins kept Adam safe.
After half an hour, the shark left, but the dolphins swam with him for another hour.

105.title: Josh's holiday
arts: Hey Josh, did you have a good holiday?
Hi Mandy, yes it was great.
Where did you go?
The Pantanal, it's in the east of Brazil. It's a really big wetland.
Oh right, so why did you go there?
Because there are amazing animals and birds there.
We all love animals in my family, especially my dad.
He's a bird watcher.
Really? I didn't know that.
Yes, he loves birds.
So are you a big bird watcher too?
Well I like them and we saw some really beautiful parrots and toucans, but I prefer the other animals.
Did you see anything special?
Yes, loads of stuff.
There were lots of Cayman.
Cayman? What are they?
They're like small crocodiles.
Cool, what else did you see?
We saw an anaconda, you know one of those really big snakes, and then one night we heard a jaguar but we didn't see it.
Wow, were you scared?
No, it was exciting, especially because it was so near our tent.
Tent? Did you go camping?
Yes, but just for a few nights. Most of the time we were in small hotels.
So how did you travel around? Did you have a guide?
Yes, we did.
His name was Sergio.
He knew where to find all the animals.
Did he speak English?
Yes, he did. His English was good which was lucky because no one in my family can speak Portuguese.
It sounds like you had a great time.
We did. It was fantastic.

106.title: Extinct animals
arts: The Great Auk
The Great Auk was a large seabird that lived in the North Atlantic.
It was a bird but it couldn't fly.
It could swim underwater really well.
It caught and ate fish when it dived under the water.
Its feathers were very soft and people used them to make pillows for their beds.
Because of this people killed the birds.
The last Great Auk died on the island of Eldey in 1835.
The Tasmanian Tiger
The Tasmanian Tiger was only found in Australia, Tasmania and New Guinea.
It got its name because it had stripes like a tiger but it was not a member of the cat family.
Farmers believed Tasmanian Tigers killed their sheep so they paid people to kill them.
Many of the tigers died after getting ill from diseases they caught from other animals.
The last Tasmanian Tiger died in Hobart Zoo in 1936.
Steller's Sea Cow
Steller's Sea Cow was a large animal that lived in the cold Arctic waters around Alaska.
It grew up to nine metres long.
Because it was so big it couldn't go under the water.
It ate the plants on top of the sea.
It wasn't a very dangerous animal.
It was quite friendly.
Because of this it was very easy to kill.
Europeans first found the sea cow in 1741.
27 years later they killed the last one.

108.title: Sequencing a story
arts: Hey Nathan, how are you? Did you have a good weekend?
Well, sort of. I mean, it was okay.
You don't sound very sure. What happened?
Yeah, come on, tell us.
Alright, well on Sundays we usually go for a walk, my family and I, but yesterday I went alone.
Where did you go?
I went to the forest, you know, outside town. It's really nice there.
And I started walking when suddenly...
Yes, suddenly what?
Well, in front of me there was a snake.
Are there snakes in the forest? Are you sure?
Yes, I'm sure. It was on the path. I stopped. I didn't do anything. Then it just went away. I was afraid.
Poor you. I hate snakes too.
Why were you afraid? It's just a snake. A snake can't kill you.
Some snakes can. Anyway, it's okay to be afraid sometimes.
Thanks Lena. Anyway, that's why my weekend was just okay.
